# Call proj from R

Status: the first M4 adapter is under development, not part of the published
R package or a complete replacement for projr. The existing R package is unchanged.

## Read a project path

The new source package is in frontends/r/projcli. It needs the separately installed
proj command plus the R packages processx and jsonlite. Installing or checking this
package never downloads proj. Install those prerequisites deliberately; then,
from a source checkout, install the adapter with R CMD INSTALL frontends/r/projcli.

~~~r
reply <- projcli::proj_cli(
  "path get", c("--label", "output", "results.csv"), project = ".")
reply$result$path
~~~

Pass each argument separately, without shell quoting. Spaces and Unicode paths
stay part of the argument. The adapter checks the command's machine interface
before sending the requested action. Set binary to an exact executable path or
options(projcli.binary = ...) when proj is not on PATH. It gives setup guidance
if the command is missing or incompatible; it does not download a replacement.

This low-level call is explicit CLI selection. Existing projr functions remain
available as an escape hatch; automatic backend routing and the familiar public
API mapping are the next M4 slice, not implemented by this transport.

## Pass credentials deliberately

The adapter forwards the active R library folders, a small baseline of system
and locale variables, and additional variables you explicitly supply in env.
It does not forward every R-session variable or copy your in-memory R objects.
During a CLI build it also preserves the two managed context values, so calls
inside R scripts keep the captured project, profile and version after changing
folders. With no explicit project argument, the CLI keeps its normal captured
root or nearest-project selection; an explicit project remains an override.
For example, a GitHub operation can receive a token explicitly from your own
configured environment; the adapter does not create or grant credentials.

Raw child diagnostics can contain secrets. This first interface discards them
and returns safe error codes rather than echoing command arguments, tokens or
arbitrary machine error text. Use the CLI directly for detailed private logs.
Requested result data is still returned; arbitrary project code is not a sandbox.
Startup files can still run. A timeout or failure may follow partial changes or
uploads, so inspect before retrying. Dependency restoration is separate, explicit
M4 work; renv is not required for every project.

## Reference and test boundary

The supported wire contract is protocol1/capability1, not an exact CLI version
match. The full validated envelope is returned as an R list. projcli_error has
safe code/status fields and no retained child output or invocation metadata.
The package manual documents the environment baseline, Windows additions, response
read limit and timeout behavior. [CRAN notes](r-wrapper-cran.qmd) explain why checks
without a CLI and required integration checks are separate; no CRAN acceptance
or full R/IDE/renderer parity is claimed.

The candidate adds unconditional malformed-response, environment, argument and
missing-binary tests, plus required real Linux/Windows checks against the separately
published, hash-verified preview.4. [PR225](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/225) records exact-head
remote results; those checks must pass before merge.
The full M4 gate still needs a named representative project, renderer/hook mapping,
explicit selected dependency preparation, archive/restore and baseline rerun comparison.


## Read configuration without reimplementing YAML (next M4 candidate)

The new projr_yml_get, projr_yml_check and projr_par_get/projr_param_get helpers use
explicit CLI queries. They need a candidate CLI advertising yml get and yml parameter;
the published preview.4 validation command cannot supply these values.

~~~r
settings <- projcli::projr_yml_get(project = ".")
seed <- projcli::projr_par_get("model", "seed", project = ".")
~~~

Keys are data, never evaluated as R code. Homogeneous scalar arrays become R vectors;
mixed/null-bearing arrays and maps stay lists, without automatic date/data-frame
conversion. Use the CLI backend's supported runtime aliases/settings; older par/pars
and R-only runtime configuration are not silently translated.

An explicit existing R function is the legacy escape hatch:

~~~r
settings <- projcli::projr_yml_get(backend = projr::projr_yml_get)
~~~

That callback runs in your R session/current folder, with its original arguments,
results and errors. It can retain the old engine's prompts, installations and other
effects; CLI redaction/isolation does not apply. The adapter does not load or install
a legacy package automatically. CLI-only project/binary/env/timeout controls cannot
be mixed into callback mode. There is no silent fallback.

The old getter's explicit profile argument reads a single layer, while CLI profiles
select merged overlays; that R argument therefore requires a callback. Old check
was ignored in the reference source; the CLI check flag actually validates. The
supported default is merged active configuration, with values read at query time.

### Supported-subset work still pending

Build/dev/path/version wrappers, renderer/hook reconciliation, repository-level
restore and explicit dependency restoration are not delivered by these getters.
The source audit found real boundaries: legacy path lookup creates folders, version
helpers may prefer DESCRIPTION, repository restore clones before restoring multiple
labels, and renv restore chooses installation sources. These are not silently equated
with read-only CLI lookup, VERSION-only authority or single-label data restore.

## Run a preview or build from R

The draft frontend also provides build, path and VERSION helpers. A preview runs
configured scripts without publishing; an explicit production bump runs the
existing CLI build workflow.

~~~r
projcli::projr_build_dev(execution_dir = "project")
projcli::projr_build_patch(msg = "Update results", execution_dir = "project")
output <- projcli::projr_path_get("output", "results.csv", format = "absolute")
dir.create(dirname(output), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
projcli::projr_version_get()
~~~

Path lookup does not create folders or rewrite renderer configuration. Choose
folder creation explicitly in your analysis. Omitting execution_dir preserves the
CLI's configured/native working-directory policy. Omitting clear_output preserves
its configured clearing policy; explicit never means none. Use configured upload
destinations rather than legacy archive switches.

This supported subset uses VERSION. DESCRIPTION-authoritative projects, Bookdown
builds, R renderer argument objects, dev version bumps and implicit folder creation
need an explicit existing R function backend. This keeps their different behavior
visible instead of silently treating it as equivalent. For example,
backend = projr::projr_build_patch calls that function in your current R session;
the old package must already be installed. No package is installed automatically.

## Share values between plain R scripts

By default each R script starts fresh. Set config.r.session to shared if a later
R script should use objects or loaded packages from an earlier one. The shared
process lasts for that build only and starts when its first plain R analysis
script runs. It is separate from your interactive R session. Hooks and rendered
documents keep their existing behavior; they do not share these objects.

To choose another installed R, set config.r.rscript to its Rscript executable
path. See the [configuration reference](configuration.qmd#r-processes-and-executable)
for working directories, startup files and supported inputs. The housekeeping
worker discussed for repeated documentation tasks is still a proposal, not this
analysis-session feature.

## Restore R packages only when you ask

For a trusted project with an existing renv.lock, create a project library and run:

~~~r
dir.create("restored-library", showWarnings = FALSE)
receipt <- projcli::proj_renv_restore(".", "restored-library")
receipt$packages
~~~

This explicit operation installs the locked dependencies using an already installed
renv package. It does not install renv, run automatically during builds, update the
lockfile, delete extra library packages or activate the project in your current R
session. Ordinary projects do not need renv. Use a disposable project copy first:
dependency installation can run package scripts and contact lockfile repositories.

Select rscript explicitly for another installed R. The default uses your current
R installation; config.r.rscript separately selects the Rust build drivers.
The receipt reports observed locked package versions and a lockfile checksum.
A failed restore is not a successful reanalysis; inspect the library/cache before
retrying. Legacy GitHub/BiocManager selectors and update helpers remain outside
this supported subset. See the package dependency reference.

## Check a real analysis after changing engines

The M4 acceptance test uses the existing Weisberger weed-study scripts 01 and 04
at a fixed public commit. It compares their complete generated CSV contents across
the old R engine and the new frontend, then archives locally, restores all selected
folders into a fresh project, restores its R packages explicitly and reruns it.

The scope is the two processing scripts and a generated test report. The test
expects 265 and 236 data rows and checks the report's visible counts. The scientific
scripts remain unchanged. It uses the same current pinned R runtime for both engines;
historical paper models and the earlier R4.1.1 environment are outside this comparison.
Its package snapshot is captured once for the run; fresh project libraries restore
from an owned cache primed from that matched environment. The separate small-package
test covers a cold, cache-disabled restore.

This heavier check is explicitly selected through representative_reanalysis in
the [R workflow](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/workflows/r-adapter.yml).
Ordinary package checks do not fetch studies or install dependencies. Retained
results contain source/package pins, hashes, row comparisons and checks; original
scripts, datasets, generated CSVs/reports and local stores are not uploaded.
